From: Elena Morris <elena@logstream.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 22 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor addition: LambdaOps (log parsing) — initial notice

Hi Jonas —

Quick heads-up: LogStream is onboarding a subprocessor, LambdaOps, to handle real-time log parsing and enrichment for our observability pipeline. They will receive structured logs (json), some application identifiers, and in limited cases debug traces that may contain user identifiers. No billing data or full PII dumps.

Per our MSA Order Form, we want to loop you in to get Redwoods' sign-off on the flow-down language and to confirm required evidence. Attached is the current orderform draft where we propose LambdaOps as a subprocessor (attachment: orderform-draft.pdf). LambdaOps has shared an SOC2 Type II (2026) and an access matrix — I can push those through if helpful.

High-level ask: what evidence and DPA language do you need to accept LambdaOps as a delegated subprocessor? Also, what internal review path / timeline should we expect (legal + procurement)?

Thanks —
Elena Morris
Head of Partnerships, LogStream Inc.
elena@logstream.io

Subject: Re: Subprocessor addition: LambdaOps (log parsing) — initial notice

Elena —

Thanks for the notice and for attaching the draft. Quick responses and a proposed path: 

1) Scope & data types: please confirm (a) whether LambdaOps receives full trace payloads or only sampled/de-identified traces and (b) if any logs include credit-card numbers, SSNs or other regulated identifiers.

2) Evidence we need up front: SOC2 Type II (latest report and bridge letter if older than 6 months), TLS+at-rest encryption description, access control matrix, list of environments (dev/stage/prod) LambdaOps will operate in, and a named point of contact for security incidents. Please provide the LambdaOps-SOC2-2026.pdf and the access matrix.

3) Contracting asks: our legal team will want: explicit subprocessor flow-down (audit rights + right to terminate for noncompliance), 30-day notice for subprocessor additions, deletion/return obligations, and a data residency statement for any EU data (if applicable). Kimberly, please advise on language we should push back with on the Order Form / MSA Annex.

4) Timeline: procurement gate (Neha + Marissa) — can we target an internal decision and DocuSign-ready package within 3 business days from receipt of the evidence above? If LambdaOps needs redlines, legal will issue a marked draft.

If you can post the SOC2 and access matrix to the Drive link or send over as attachments, that will speed things up.

I'll stand up a short triage call if needed.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Platform Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Subprocessor addition: LambdaOps — proposed redlines and needs

Team —

I reviewed the SOC2 and access matrix. High-level legal guidance and proposed actions: 

- Insert/require an explicit Subprocessor Flow-Down clause in the Order Form: LambdaOps must be bound by the same DPA obligations as Redwood to the customer (audit cooperation, data deletion, sub-subprocessor restriction).
- Audit rights: include right for Redwood (and, where contractually required, our customers) to perform audits or to receive SOC2 reports and remediation plans. If LambdaOps insists on routed requests, we need SLAs for response time (5 business days to acknowledge, 15 business days for initial evidence).
- Notification timeline: require 30 days' prior notice for additional subprocessors, with emergency exception and immediate notice for security incidents.
- Termination: if material noncompliance, Redwood must have explicit termination rights for the portion of services involving LambdaOps; include mapping for transition assistance.
- Data handling & retention: require deletion or return of data within 30 days of contract end and documentation of deletion.

I have prepared a short clause bundle — redwood_subproc_clause_v2.docx — to propose to LogStream/LambdaOps. Procurement, please confirm if we can live with SOC2 + attestations + access matrix for now, and we will push the clause in the redline. If LambdaOps accepts the clause bundle, legal is fine to proceed down DocuSign.

Jonas — can you confirm whether any EU data flows through this integration? If yes we will need a stronger residency statement.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
